relationships.title: Divine Thunder
relationships.description: Zeus commands the Lightning Bolt, his signature weapon that strikes down mortals and immortals alike with the fury of the heavens.

relationships.title: Hammer of Thunder
relationships.description: Thor's mighty hammer Mjolnir can only be lifted by those worthy, and returns to his hand after every throw, channeling the power of storms.

relationships.title: Cycle of Rebirth
relationships.description: The Phoenix rises from the Eternal Flame, reborn from its own ashes in an endless cycle of death and resurrection.

relationships.title: Dragon's Breath
relationships.description: Dragons breathe the Eternal Flame, an ancient fire that burns hotter than any mortal flame and can melt the strongest metals.

relationships.title: Divine Punishment
relationships.description: Athena cursed Medusa, transforming her beautiful hair into serpents and giving her the power to turn anyone who meets her gaze to stone.

relationships.title: King of Gods
relationships.description: Zeus rules all gods from his throne atop Mount Olympus, the highest peak where mortals cannot reach and gods hold their councils.

relationships.title: Shield Maidens
relationships.description: The Valkyries serve the Norse gods, choosing which warriors will die in battle and escorting the worthy to Valhalla.

relationships.title: Divine Craftsmanship
relationships.description: Excalibur was blessed by Athena, goddess of wisdom and warfare, granting it unbreakable strength and the ability to cut through any armor.

relationships.title: Deep Terror
relationships.description: The Kraken emerges from the darkest depths of the Underworld's oceans, a monstrous beast that drags ships to their doom.

relationships.title: Guardian of the Dead
relationships.description: Anubis guards the Underworld, weighing the hearts of the deceased against the feather of truth to determine their eternal fate.

relationships.title: Fire and Rebirth
relationships.description: The Phoenix and Dragon are eternal rivals, both masters of flame but representing opposing forces of destruction and renewal.

relationships.title: Storm Weapons
relationships.description: Both the Lightning Bolt and Mjolnir channel the raw power of storms, though one strikes from the sky while the other is hurled by hand.

relationships.title: Divine Lineage
relationships.description: Zeus is the father of Athena, who sprang fully formed from his head, inheriting his wisdom and becoming goddess of strategic warfare.

relationships.title: Norse vs Greek
relationships.description: The Valkyries of Norse mythology stand in contrast to the gods of Olympus, representing different cultural interpretations of divine power.

relationships.title: Eternal Exile
relationships.description: Medusa was banished to the edges of the Underworld, dwelling in darkness where her cursed gaze could harm no innocent souls.

relationships.title: Dragon Slayer
relationships.description: Excalibur has slain countless dragons, its divine edge capable of piercing even the thickest dragon scales.

relationships.title: Sacred Fire
relationships.description: The Eternal Flame burns perpetually in the temples of Mount Olympus, a symbol of the gods' immortal power.

relationships.title: Thunder Gods
relationships.description: Thor and Zeus are parallel deities from different pantheons, both commanding thunder and lightning as kings of their respective realms.

relationships.title: Divine Wisdom
relationships.description: Anubis and Athena share a mutual respect as deities of wisdom and judgment, though they serve different pantheons and purposes.

relationships.title: Titans of Destruction
relationships.description: When the Kraken and Dragon meet, their battle shakes the earth and sea, two unstoppable forces of nature clashing in epic combat.
